text:
Evidence supports interaction-aware text representations, but evidence for the exact proposed setup—GRU4Rec plus jointly trained, randomly initialized title/description encoder and ID embeddings—is limited. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) integrates item text with ID and positional embeddings, but uses pretrained BERT and reviews; its results do not establish effectiveness under this task’s restrictions. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) reports improvements in low-resource and cold-start recommendation using learned textual representations. However, its Transformer architecture and pretraining procedure differ substantially from a category-local GRU trained from scratch; its ablations also show that pretraining matters.

The central concern is semantic–behavioral mismatch: similar descriptions need not imply similar next-item demand. [CASG (2026)](https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-main.2001/) reports that text embeddings can underperform learned IDs and benefits from guiding representations with collaborative relationships, although it uses frozen text encoders rather than the proposed setup. A defensible experiment is therefore one jointly trained GRU network: combine ID embeddings with a small shared token encoder over available titles/descriptions, learning both through next-item supervision. Shared tokens could transfer interaction evidence to rare items; preserving numbers and model identifiers could help distinguish specifications. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated compatibility guarantees. Evaluate against the corrected ID-only GRU using the pinned macro validation HR@10, with training-frequency diagnostics to determine whether rare items benefit. No located evidence establishes that textual similarity alone captures compatibility or current need.
